blocks.content: Instructions: Each question carries 1 mark. Negative marking: –0.25 for wrong answers. Choose the most appropriate answer.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Section A tests historical events, dynasties, and key movements in Uttarakhand across Questions 1 to 20.
Section B assesses geographical knowledge including rivers, mountains, and administrative divisions in Questions 21 to 40.
Section C covers regional culture, state governance structures, and mixed topic practice in Questions 41 to 60.
The chapter provides a total set of 60 practice multiple-choice questions for state competitive exam preparation.

blocks.content: Q.1 Which dynasty first unified the 52 Garhwal principalities into a single kingdom?
Answer: (C) | Raja Ajay Pal of the Parmar/Panwar dynasty unified the 52 Garh principalities (Bawan Garh) in the early 16th century.
Q.2 Who founded the Chand Dynasty of Kumaon?
Answer: (B) | Raja Som Chand founded the Chand dynasty around 700–900 CE at Champawat.
Q.3 The Treaty of Sugauli (1816) was signed between:
(A) British East India Company and Tehri Garhwal
(B) British East India Company and Nepal
Answer: (B) | The Treaty of Sugauli ended the Anglo-Nepalese War (1814–16); Nepal ceded Kumaon and eastern Garhwal to the British.
Q.4 Which Garhwal king died fighting the Gurkhas in 1804 near Dehra Dun?
Answer: (C) | Raja Pradyumna Shah died at the battle of Khurbura near Dehra Dun in 1804 fighting the Gurkhas.
Q.5 The anti-Begar (forced labour) movement in Uttarakhand was launched at which fair in 1921?
Answer: (B) | Badridutt Pandey organised the Begar abolition movement at the Uttarayani Fair in Bageshwar on January 14, 1921.
Q.6 Vir Chandra Singh Garhwali is famous for:
(B) Refusing to fire on Pathans during Peshawar Conspiracy Case 1930
Answer: (B) | Chandra Singh Garhwali of the Royal Garhwal Rifles refused to fire on unarmed Pathans in Peshawar in April 1930.
Q.7 The Tilari Massacre of 1930 occurred in:
Answer: (B) | On May 30, 1930, protesters were shot in Tehri Garhwal princely state during an anti-ruler demonstration — often compared to Jallianwala Bagh.
Q.8 Uttarakhand was carved out of which state?
Answer: (C) | Uttarakhand (Uttaranchal) was carved out of Uttar Pradesh on November 9, 2000.
Q.9 Who was the first Chief Minister of Uttaranchal (Uttarakhand)?
Answer: (D) | Nityanand Swami (BJP) was the first CM of Uttaranchal on Nov 9, 2000.
Q.10 On which date is Uttarakhand Statehood Day (Sthapna Diwas) celebrated?
Answer: (B) | Uttaranchal was formed on November 9, 2000; this date is celebrated as Uttarakhand Sthapna Diwas.
Q.11 Gairsain (Bhararisain) was declared the summer capital of Uttarakhand in:
Answer: (D) | CM Trivendra Singh Rawat declared Gairsain (Bhararisain) in Chamoli as the summer capital in March 2020.
Q.12 The Rampur Tiraha firing incident of October 2, 1994 is remembered as:
Answer: (B) | The Rampur Tiraha firing (Muzaffarnagar) on October 2, 1994 killed Uttarakhand statehood agitators; it is remembered as Krantiveer Shaurya Diwas.
Q.13 Which king of Garhwal was restored to western Garhwal after the Anglo-Nepalese War?
Answer: (C) | Sudarshan Shah, son of Pradyumna Shah, was given western Garhwal (Tehri Garhwal) as a princely state after the 1816 treaty.
Q.14 The Uttarakhand Kranti Dal, a major party driving statehood, was founded in:
Answer: (C) | The Uttarakhand Kranti Dal was founded in 1979 as the primary regional party demanding statehood.
Q.15 Govind Ballabh Pant, who was India's Home Minister and received Bharat Ratna, was born in which district of Uttarakhand?
Answer: (B) | G.B. Pant was born in Khoont village, Almora district, in 1887.
Q.16 The Chipko Movement of 1973 began in which village of Chamoli?
Answer: (C) | Gaura Devi led villagers of Reni village, Chamoli, to hug trees and prevent felling in April 1973 — the starting point of the Chipko Movement.
Q.17 Who was the first woman to lead the Chipko protest at Reni village?
Answer: (B) | Gaura Devi mobilised women of Reni village to physically hug trees on March 26, 1974 (Reni protest), inspired by earlier Chipko events.
Answer: (C) | The state was officially renamed from Uttaranchal to Uttarakhand on January 1, 2007.
Q.19 Henry Ramsay served as Commissioner of Kumaon for approximately:
Answer: (C) | Henry Ramsay served as Commissioner of Kumaon from 1856 to 1884 — approximately 37 years — and had a significant impact on administration.
Q.20 Sumitranandan Pant, the famous Hindi poet, was born in:
Answer: (B) | Sumitranandan Pant was born in Kausani, Almora district, in 1900.
Q.21 The highest peak entirely within India is located in Uttarakhand. Name it.
Answer: (B) | Nanda Devi (7816 m) is the highest peak located entirely within India, in Chamoli district.
Q.22 The Ganga originates at the confluence of which two rivers?
Answer: (B) | The Ganga is formed at Devprayag by the confluence of the Bhagirathi (from Gangotri) and Alaknanda rivers.
Answer: (B) | The Alaknanda originates from Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers near Badrinath.
Q.24 Hemkund Sahib (Gurudwara) is situated at an altitude of approximately:
Answer: (C) | Hemkund Sahib is located at 4329 m (some sources say 4361 m) in Chamoli district.
Q.25 Which lake in Uttarakhand is famous for unidentified skeletal remains?
Answer: (C) | Roopkund Lake (4800 m), Chamoli district, is known as the 'Mystery Lake' for human skeletons found on its shores.
Q.26 The Gangotri Glacier is the source of which river?
Answer: (D) | The Bhagirathi river originates from the Gaumukh glacial cave at the snout of the Gangotri Glacier.
Q.27 Panch Prayag refers to five confluences on the Alaknanda system. Which is the last (downstream) one where Ganga is formed?
Answer: (C) | At Devprayag (Tehri Garhwal), Alaknanda meets Bhagirathi to form the Ganga — the final Panch Prayag.
Q.28 Uttarakhand shares an international border with which two countries?
Answer: (C) | Uttarakhand borders China (Tibet) in the north and Nepal in the east.
Q.29 The Bugiyal in Uttarakhand refers to:
Answer: (B) | Bugiyal (also Bugyal) are high-altitude (3500–4500 m) alpine meadows used for seasonal grazing — unique to the Garhwal Himalayas.
Q.30 Doodhatoli Hills are associated with the origin of which river?
Answer: (C) | The Western Ramganga originates in the Dudhatoli hills (Chamoli/Almora border region).
Q.31 The Lipulekh Pass is significant because it connects India to Tibet and lies at the trijunction of:
Answer: (A) | Lipulekh Pass (5334 m) in Pithoragarh lies at the trijunction of India, Nepal, and China and is on the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra route.
Q.32 Valley of Flowers National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in:
Answer: (B) | Valley of Flowers NP is located in Chamoli district; it became a UNESCO WHS in 2005 (combined with Nanda Devi NP).
Q.33 The largest National Park in Uttarakhand by area is:
Answer: (C) | Gangotri National Park in Uttarkashi district covers 2390 sq km — the largest NP in Uttarakhand.
Q.34 Jim Corbett National Park was established in 1936 as:
Answer: (C) | Jim Corbett was originally established in 1936 as Hailey National Park — the first national park of India.
Q.35 Khatling Glacier is the source of which river?
Answer: (B) | The Bhilangana river originates from the Khatling Glacier in Tehri Garhwal district.
Q.36 The 'Dun' valleys in Uttarakhand are formed by:
(B) Tectonic movements between Shiwalik and Lesser Himalayas
Answer: (B) | Dun valleys (like Dehradun) are intermontane valleys formed by tectonic movements between the Shiwalik hills and the Lesser Himalayas.
Q.37 The 'Terai' region in Uttarakhand is primarily found in which districts?
Answer: (B) | The Terai — the flat fertile plain — is primarily in Haridwar and Udham Singh Nagar districts of Uttarakhand.
Q.38 Nanda Devi National Park was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
Answer: (B) | Nanda Devi National Park was inscribed as a UNESCO Natural World Heritage Site in 1988.
Q.39 Which pass is historically associated with the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra route?
Answer: (C) | Lipulekh Pass in Pithoragarh is the traditional route for the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra.
Q.40 The state animal of Uttarakhand is:
Answer: (C) | The Alpine Musk Deer (Moschus leucogaster) is the state animal of Uttarakhand.
Q.41 The traditional folk art of Kumaon involving rice paste designs on floors and walls is called:
Answer: (B) | Aipan is the traditional Kumaoni folk art using rice paste on red background, applied at doorsteps and during festivals. It has a GI tag.
Q.42 Chholiya dance of Kumaon is traditionally performed at:
Answer: (C) | Chholiya (sword and shield dance) is performed primarily during wedding processions in Kumaon.
Q.43 The Nanda Devi Raj Jat Yatra is held every:
Answer: (D) | Nanda Devi Raj Jat Yatra is held every 12 years; it is a 280 km pilgrimage procession through Chamoli and Almora.
Q.44 Harela festival in Kumaon is associated with:
Answer: (B) | Harela ('green day') is celebrated in Shravan (July) and involves sowing seeds in soil/pots at home; germinated seedlings are worshipped.
Q.45 The Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly has how many seats?
Answer: (B) | The Uttarakhand Vidhan Sabha has 70 seats (55 general, 13 SC reserved, 2 ST reserved).
Q.46 The High Court of Uttarakhand is located in:
Answer: (C) | The Uttarakhand High Court is located in Nainital; it was established on November 9, 2000.
Q.47 The Uttarakhand PSC (UKPSC) is located in:
Answer: (B) | The Uttarakhand Public Service Commission (UKPSC) is headquartered in Haridwar.
Q.48 India's first Agricultural University was established at Pantnagar in:
Answer: (C) | G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology at Pantnagar was established in 1960 as India's first agricultural university.
Q.49 Tehri Dam is built across which river?
Answer: (C) | Tehri Dam is built on the Bhagirathi river in Tehri Garhwal district; Stage I capacity is 1000 MW.
Q.50 Which is the smallest district by area in Uttarakhand?
Answer: (C) | Champawat is the smallest district in Uttarakhand with an area of 1766 sq km.
Q.51 The state bird of Uttarakhand is:

items: History questions frequently focus on key historical movements, dynastic rule, and state formation chronology in Uttarakhand.
Geography items emphasize physical features, national parks, river systems, and district-level facts.
Culture and Governance questions regularly test state symbols, administrative setup, traditional art forms, and local festivals.

blocks.content: Answer: (B) | The Himalayan Monal (Lophophorus impejanus), locally called 'Danphe' or 'Monal', is the state bird of Uttarakhand.
Q.52 Phool Dei is a spring festival of Kumaon celebrated in:
Answer: (C) | Phool Dei is celebrated in Chaitra (March), marking the onset of spring; girls place flower petals at doorsteps for blessings.
Q.53 Which institution trains IAS officers in Uttarakhand?
Answer: (C) | The Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA) in Mussoorie trains IAS and other civil service officers.
Q.54 Kainchi Dham, associated with Neem Karoli Baba, is located near:
Answer: (B) | Kainchi Dham ashram of Neem Karoli Baba (Maharaj-ji) is located at Bhowali, near Nainital.
Q.55 The Tungnath temple, the highest Shiva temple in the world, is in which district?
Answer: (C) | Tungnath (3680 m) is in Rudraprayag district; it is the second of the Panch Kedar and the world's highest Shiva temple.
Q.56 The Uttarakhand Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill was passed by the state assembly in:
Answer: (C) | The UCC Bill was passed by the Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly in February 2024, making it the first state to pass UCC.
Q.57 Jageshwar temple complex in Almora is built in which architectural style?
Answer: (C) | Jageshwar (a group of 124 temples) is built in the Nagara style; the temples date from the 7th–14th centuries.
Q.58 G.B. Pant National Himalayan Environment Institute is located in:
Answer: (B) | GB Pant National Himalayan Environment Institute (GBPNIHE) is located at Kosi-Katarmal, Almora.
Q.59 The Devidhura Mela in Champawat is known for which traditional practice?
(B) Stone pelting (Bagwal) — now replaced by flowers
Answer: (B) | Devidhura Mela features the traditional 'Bagwal' — ritual stone pelting between two groups; this has been largely replaced by flower throwing to reduce injuries.
Q.60 Uttarakhand's state flower, Brahma Kamal (Saussurea obvallata), blooms:
(B) Only in summer at lower altitudes
(C) Primarily at night in high-altitude meadows during July–September
Answer: (C) | Brahma Kamal blooms at high altitudes (3000–4800 m) primarily during July to September, and flowers bloom at night.
